A short but sweet game that may be especially interesting for people new to the command line / terminal interface. While the 'hacking' is somewhat shallow, the story is interesting. Intense time-pressure situations force you to apply your new knowledge, and fast; you must find, copy, delete, modify, scan, etc. before you're traced. It feels great to build up new hacking programs; Hacknet reveals its secrets at a natural pace.

The early missions are basic, to help you warm up your execution speed. When missions become complex (breadcrumb trails from one computer to the next), take unexpected turns, or introduce surprising new concepts and goals, Hacknet becomes truly excellent. It is not a stretch to say that the entire purpose of Hacknet is to prepare you for three or four outstanding missions - if the regular missions are engaging, these special ones inspire everything from terror to intense focus: they strain your hacking speed, your memory as you piece together a puzzle of scattered info, and inspire that conspiratorial feeling of getting closer to the hidden truth.

Hacknet doesn't outstay its welcome - it ends when all the available mechanics have been thoroughly explored and challenged, and no later. The campaign can be cleared in about six hours, and the remaining secrets and alternate paths can be tackled in another three hours (postgame knowledge and skills allow you to blast through the early missions in minutes, on subsequent playthroughs - this also feels great). 

Though its short length and limited replayability keep Hacknet out of 'classic territory', I would recommend it as a fun, fast way to get familiar with the basic concepts of terminal navigation and file editing(!). [Note: I was familiar with terminals before playing]

Hints for new players: 
1.) Don't forget about 'ps' and 'kill', they may save your life.

2.) If you find yourself in contact with a new faction or individual you want to follow-up with, do not complete or initiate missions with any other factions. [i]Completing one faction's mission while multiple paths are available will lock you into that faction's path[/i], closing off the others. [spoiler]You'll eventually end up in CSEC, no matter what[/spoiler]

3.) Use addNote for the tough stuff, but try to use your own memory whenever you can. It never hurts to download a file so you have a password on record.

4.) When in doubt, 'dc'.

I normally don't like puzzle games, because eventually a puzzle loses me once and then I never get back into the groove. Hacknet is possibly the first puzzle game that I have enjoyed since the days of Popcap. It helps that it is usually very easy, as long as you have experience with computers, and gives you specific instructions as to how to beat the levels beyond "hack everything you can". 
I have only two gripes. First is that the RAM management aspect (you only have a limited amount of ram, so you have to figure out the best parallel computing strategies when you're under a time limit) also cuts into your note-taking extensively. A single paragraph of notes takes up so much RAM that you can only use the smaller programs until you get it out of your face. The boss level fell flat as a pancake after I lost because I couldn't remember the name of a program that I needed and the list I had written for just such an occasion was deleted for taking up too much RAM. Why even have notes make such an impact on RAM economy if the player can just open up the notepad on his real desktop and use that?
Besides that bizarre choice, the network UI is appaling. In the screenshots, all those dots in the bottom of the screen are computers, there is no way to see what they are without mousing over them, you can't move them around, and they frequently overlap each other. That's another way the boss level fell flat: I just quit midway through because I had accidentally spent half the timer hacking the server that it had been placed on top of. You are just expected to remember where everything is, which wasn't easy when I had another game session the very next day, so I bet it's hellish if you have to wait a week to get back into it.
As for the good parts, it is very cool that you can play the entire game through console if you want to. Of particular note are the commands to open and close the CD tray. Apparently they actually work, even in multiplayer. There's even a branching storyline, as well as a substantial library of mods which are still being added to to this day. If you like the gameplay, then you can keep going until you don't anymore without having to retread the same ground more than a few times.

I don’t know why it’s taken me so long to get around to playing Hacknet, but now I’m kicking myself for not playing it sooner. I have not felt this engaged in an investigative simulation since I played The Black Watchmen and I really hope to find more games like this.

Hacknet is definitely a game for certain types of people, but you don’t need to have extensive IT experience to play. I think gamers who are already comfortable using command prompt will feel at home with this sim, but the game’s tutorial does a good job of walking you through the concepts and gameplay basics while still leaving you free to get creative with how to implement the tools at your disposal. Nobody is going to learn to be a [i]real[/i] hacker by playing this game, but it’s a fun introduction to the ideas behind the process and it’s immersive enough that you feel like you’re really involved with the story.

Hacknet is at its core a mystery game and your task is to track down what happened to a mysterious person who contacts you. As you work your way across the shadowy world of IP addresses, you are given more abilities and greater challenges to tinker with. I never felt that any of the tasks were impossible -- it was always that I just missed something or overlooked a scan or available command. Fast typists will have a much easier time of playing as there are frequent timers counting down in the guise of tracers.

I absolutely 100% recommend that you pick up the DLC Labyrinths. It pretty much adds an entire game campaign where you get to expand on your skills using new situations. You can play the DLC any time while still keeping your progress with the main game. Seriously, worth the extra few bucks if you can swing it.

An absolutely engaging and wonderful game. This is one of those gems that lingers in your library for a while ominously taunting you. I'm going to break this review up in a few sections. The game lets you explore what it's like to be a hacker. Well more of a stereotypical movie meme hacker, but still that's a perk here. You should expect to be snooping into people's computers, reading their emails, and finding all of their dirty secrets. With that in mind this game plays more like an information-gathering puzzle simulator.

1. Gameplay
This may be the biggest "fear" new players may have after viewing the trailer. This game involves typing out commands in a terminal, but really it's just similar to a "text based" adventure with commands. If you're new to using a CMD line (terminal) this is a perfect engaging way to become more familiar with how it works. Just like any new game once you get familiar with the controls you'll breeze through it. There is a clean graphic user interface that makes navigating the game environment (with your mouse) very intuitive. You are taught how to play in a standard tutorial so you're not just thrown out into the ocean expecting to be a 1337 h@ck0r. You will encounter several high and low points that will continue to test what you've learned. At no point in the game did I feel like it was repetitive. You will have time to become familiar with your tools and soon after your tools will grow, allowing you to tackle harder and more complex hacker challenges. 

2. Story
No spoilers. I can say that there is a story and that you will be highly involved with in. There is a lot of mysteries, and plenty of interesting characters to learn about. I should mention that each new play through of the game will have many events randomized. In addition the story continues in the DLC and that I found it totally worth it.

3. Graphics
I find the graphics to be a nice blend between modern techno sci-fi and retro website design. It's actually quite an interesting blend of styles that seems to work out well. I can safely say this [b]isn't[/b] just a game where you look into singular black box and type commands. 

4. Final Thoughts
It's good. I personally had some doubts but once I started playing I couldn't stop. I wouldn't be leaving a review if I didn't think it deserved more attention.

HACKNET is a game that surprised me. There are a lot of aspects of this game that I liked and some I didn't like about the game.

I'll start off listing the positives: 
+ A great intro to those interested in the command line interface. The tutorial makes the learning curve effortless.
+ Story was just above average, both DLC and main game. I would've really enjoyed seeing more story telling and character development. 
+ Gameplay had its moments that really surprised me and I haven't seen it used in any other games before.
+ Soundtrack was perfect for this type of game. (Much respect for the song "HOME - Resonance" being played in-game)
+ Game progression was rewarding and I was always excited to come back to where I left off. 
+ DLC was practically a new game which was another 5-6 hours of game play.


Here are some negatives that come to mind:
- Game play may feel a bit repetitive when doing missions and hacking ports. 
- While playing the main story and DLC a few times I felt lost what to do next or where I left off.
- A few mechanics felt clunky, which broke immersion occasionally. 
- Accidentally deleting an important file in-game will practically break your game. 

I got this game for free last year on the Humble Bundle store, I didn't expect much from it because it was free but I finally gave it a shot this summer and I was blown away how much fun it was. If you are interested in programming or computers in general I highly recommend trying this game out. 


Overall this is a uniquely great game and I do recommend it to those who have an interest in computers and coding.

My Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐✨ 4 / 5

10/10 game, if you're into simulation games that simulate what hacking actually is like. The music is great, the story, while minimal, is great in my opinion. And whenever a game makes me feel great about finishing it, it's a solid game. 
tl;dr Buy it if you like typing and good music
